D.t: Hannah Pingree leads by 12.6 in the forecast and wins 98% of simulations. The cushion is about 93,269 votes; a one point swing is about 3,704 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +5.0 and D +20.0. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +11.5. Your best recent poll is Maine People's Resource Center (D) at D +14.3; your worst is Marist College at R +2.0. 13 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Cumberland, a projected net 77,928 votes; York, a projected net 20,708 votes; Knox, a projected net 6,014 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Penobscot, R +6.8, 10.4% of the vote; Kennebec, D +1.7, 8.9% of the vote; Androscoggin, R +1.7, 7.1% of the vote; Oxford, R +8.1, 4.1% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Hannah Pingree runs furthest behind in Aroostook, Piscataquis, Somerset. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 95% of voters, 51 to 40, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.75 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 77% of voters, 53 to 39, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.84 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 63% of voters, 54 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.13 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Hannah Pingree: Immigration voters 15 to 76, Men 45 to 46, Midsize counties 47 to 45. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$1.2M cash against $395K. Spend it early on persuasion television in the battleground counties and keep a reserve for the last week.
Registered Democrats cast 48% of the 244,931 ballots in Maine so far, against 22% for the other party. That is 0.3 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 0.4 points away from Hannah Pingree. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
Activity: 5 campaign stops by the candidate or surrogates in 30 days.

R.t: Bobby Charles trails by 12.6 and wins 2% of simulations. Closing it takes about 46,635 voters switching sides, or 93,269 more net votes from new turnout.

The polls page average is D +11.5. Your best recent poll is Marist College at R +2.0; your worst is Maine People's Resource Center (D) at D +14.3. 13 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Republicans: Aroostook, a projected net 7,918 votes; Somerset, a projected net 6,057 votes; Penobscot, a projected net 5,238 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Penobscot, R +6.8, 10.4% of the vote; Kennebec, D +1.7, 8.9% of the vote; Androscoggin, R +1.7, 7.1% of the vote; Oxford, R +8.1, 4.1% of the vote.

R.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
R.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Bobby Charles runs furthest behind in Cumberland, York. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 95% of voters, 40 to 51, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.75 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 77% of voters, 39 to 53, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.84 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 63% of voters, 37 to 54, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.13 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Bobby Charles: Large counties 24 to 68, Health care and Social Security voters 24 to 67, Corruption voters 27 to 65. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$395K cash against $1.2M. Outspent: lean on earned media, digital, field and the outside groups, and pick the two or three media markets that decide it.
